summary: Confirmed PARTIAL. 60633eff3 (#710) replaced the per-scope Map with an LRUCache (64 queries, 2 MiB). It also added exact local narrowing: when a fresh, complete (not truncated, not partial) result exists for a prefix, the query is reranked on the client with the same shared rankWorkspaceEntries the server uses, and the composer skips its 120 ms debounce for it. I checked that narrowing is exact. Every match tier implies a subsequence match, the server indexes with normalizedPath = path.toLowerCase(), the tie-break is the path, and the limit is the scope's limit. Pre-fix servers used the same predicate and scoring for non-empty queries, so they stay compatible. Results flagged refreshing are never cached. No Hub-side or alternative implementation exists; the Hub vendors Ryco 7bc39eec3, which already contains 60633eff3. Still missing: proposal 3 (the listEntries or relay-local search, a shorter debounce, and a server-pushed index-change invalidation). Also missing is a small part of proposal 1: entries older than staleTime are never dropped. They are only evicted under LRU pressure within the same scope. Scope runtimes are never pruned outside hosted teardown, so total memory is bounded per scope but not across scopes.

evidence.note: PROJECT_SEARCH_ENTRIES_CACHE_MAX_QUERIES = 64 and MAX_BYTES = 2 MiB (line 21). LRUCache is built at 180-183, and writes at 355 and 404 pass estimateResultBytes (238).
readFreshCacheEntry treats entries older than staleTime (15 s) as misses but never deletes them. Only LRU pressure from a new insert into the same scope evicts them.

narrowFromCache walks prefixes from longest to shortest, including the empty query. It stops if the nearest fresh prefix is truncated or partial, reranks with the shared ranker otherwise, and keeps the prefix's fetchedAt, so freshness is not extended.
requestProjectSearchEntries tries the exact cache, then narrowing, then the server. A local answer bumps the token so older in-flight responses cannot overwrite it.

As before the fix, cache.set runs before the token check and there is no invalidation-generation fence. A response computed before an invalidation can repopulate the cache after it, and narrowing would serve its extensions for up to 15 s. The window is tiny: CheckpointReactor.ts:540 invalidates the server index before the turn-diff event, and dirty indexes answer with refreshing=true, which is never cached.

scopeRuntimes (and the keepAlive state atoms at 115) are only cleared by clearProjectAtomState. Its only non-test caller is the hosted Hub environment teardown (apps/web/src/hostedHub/environment.ts:47). Desktop and local web keep a scope for every env+cwd (including worktrees) where the @ menu was opened, together with its up to 64 stale entries.

canResolveProjectSearchEntriesLocally bypasses the debounce for locally answerable queries. Anything else still waits the fixed COMPOSER_PATH_QUERY_DEBOUNCE_MS = 120 (line 48, used at 107-111), with no relay-aware value.

truncated = index.partial || matchedCount > limit (80). Narrowing therefore applies only once a prefix has 80 or fewer matches, so short prefixes in large repos still pay debounce plus RTT (a relay round trip when hosted).

scoreWorkspaceEntry is shared by the server and the client narrowing. The empty query ranks by depth*2+kind, so a complete '' result (an index of 80 entries or fewer) is the whole index and narrowing from it is exact.

projectListEntriesQuery is used only by the files tree (useProjectPreview.ts). Its staleTime is 0 (line 15), it is not invalidated on turn diffs, and the server caps it at WORKSPACE_LIST_ENTRIES_MAX = 25_000 shallowest entries (WorkspaceEntries.ts:80), marking it truncated beyond that. The composer never searches it.
Client invalidation is still inferred from thread.turn-diff-completed and thread.reverted, scoped per checkout cwd. There is no server-pushed index-changed signal.
Out of scope but related: the mobile searchEntries query is already bounded (retainedKeyLimit 30), but it has no narrowing.

remaining: 1) Proposal 3 (M, optional) is not done. (a) No local search over cached listEntries data or on hosted relay connections: requestProjectSearchEntries (projectAtoms.ts:385) consults only its own search cache, and projectListEntriesQuery (projectPreviewAtoms.ts:112) is used only by the files tree. (b) Queries that cannot be answered locally still use a fixed 120 ms debounce (ComposerAttachmentMenus.tsx:48, 107-111), on relay connections too. (c) No server push of index changes. Invalidation is client-inferred (projectSearchInvalidation.ts:54), and listEntries has staleTime 0 with no turn-diff invalidation, so a local index copy needs its own freshness policy. 2) Part of proposal 1 is missing (S): entries older than staleTime are never dropped (projectAtoms.ts:246 only skips them), and scope runtimes and state atoms are never pruned outside hosted teardown (projectAtoms.ts:113, 795). Each scope is capped at 64 entries (about 1 MB at roughly 16 KB per 80-entry result), but an idle worktree scope keeps unservable stale entries for the whole session and the number of scopes has no limit. Both items are low impact.
fixDefects: No correctness defects. Narrowing is exact: it uses the shared ranker, server normalizedPath equals path.toLowerCase(), the tie-break is the path, fetchedAt is preserved, refreshing results are never cached, and pre-fix servers used the same predicate for non-empty queries. Two minor hardening points. (1) startFetch writes into the cache before its token check, with no invalidation generation (projectAtoms.ts:354-356), which was already the case before the fix. Narrowing widens the effect: a response computed before invalidateProjectSearchEntries can be re-cached afterwards and then answer every extension of its query for up to 15 s. The server makes this nearly impossible by invalidating before emitting the turn-diff event and flagging dirty answers as refreshing. (2) canResolveProjectSearchEntriesLocally runs narrowFromCache during render (reranking at most 80 entries and promoting LRU entries), and requestProjectSearchEntries repeats the work in the effect. The cost is negligible.
implementationSketch: A) Pruning (S, no decision needed). In apps/web/src/rpc/projectAtoms.ts, when releaseProjectSearchEntriesScope drops observerCount to 0, start one timer per runtime for staleTime (15 s); if observerCount is still 0 when it fires, call runtime.cache.clear(), because nothing older than staleTime can ever be served. Optionally cap scopeRuntimes to about 16 idle scopes in LRU order: delete idle runtimes beyond the cap and reset their state atoms the way clearProjectAtomState does. Add a per-runtime `generation` that invalidateProjectSearchEntries increments; startFetch captures it and skips cache.set when it has changed. Tests in projectAtoms.test.ts: a release followed by vi.advanceTimersByTime(15_000) leaves the cache empty (the next request hits the server); a response that resolves after an invalidation is not cached and is not used for narrowing. B) Local listing source (M, needs a decision). Add resolveListingSearch(environmentId, cwd, query, limit) to projectAtoms.ts or a new apps/web/src/rpc/projectLocalSearch.ts. It reads the projectListEntriesQuery state for env+cwd from the atom registry and uses it only when data exists and truncated === false. It memoizes the search keys per listing object in a WeakMap, as {path, kind, normalizedPath: path.toLowerCase(), entry: {path, kind, parentPath: workspaceEntryParentPath(path)}}, and ranks them with rankWorkspaceEntries, returning truncated = matchedCount > limit. Call it from requestProjectSearchEntries after the cache and narrowing misses, and from canResolveProjectSearchEntriesLocally. No worker is needed, because listEntries is capped at 25k entries and ranking that many measured 2.3-8.6 ms. Freshness: invalidate or refresh projectListEntriesQuery from the same ProjectSearchInvalidationQueue flush (per env+cwd), and treat the listing as a local source only within the search staleTime of its fetch. Optionally, on relay connections (the transport kind comes from the client-runtime connection catalog), prefetch listEntries when the @ menu opens. The proper fix for out-of-band edits is a server push of index generation changes (a new orchestration or workspace push in packages/contracts plus ws.ts), but the client-side invalidation reuse is enough for a first step. Tests: unit-test that listing-based results equal server-ranked results for the same entries (reuse the WorkspaceEntries fixtures), that a truncated listing is ignored, and that invalidation drops the listing source; extend ComposerAttachmentMenus coverage so a locally resolvable query skips the debounce.
decisionReason: Only part B (proposal 3) needs a decision. Answering @-search from a client copy of the full index trades bandwidth and memory for latency. On hosted relays that means prefetching up to 25k entries through the E2EE relay, which is capped at 4 MiB per RPC message. It also changes freshness semantics: listEntries has staleTime 0, no turn-diff invalidation, and no server push. Robust invalidation needs a new server-pushed index-change signal in contracts/ws, a protocol addition, not a Hub change. Part A (pruning and the generation fence) is local and needs no decision.
